headline: Symmetries, Codes, and Diagnostics in Quantum Systems
summary: Today's papers explore structural simplifications across quantum information, from classifying topological CSS codes to learning dense Clifford-structured Hamiltonians. Highlights include drastically compressing neural quantum state models using symmetry constraints and advanced physical diagnostics for silicon T centers and optical lattices.

themes.title: Topological CSS Codes & Classification
themes.body: New results analyze translation-invariant CSS quantum error-correcting codes, proving 2D variants decouple into standard toric codes while introducing homological Koszul-complex tools to probe 3D topological rigidity and superselection profiles.

themes.title: Quantum Learning & Structural Compression
themes.body: Exploiting structural constraints enables dramatically lower learning complexity, whether compressing neural quantum states from thousands of parameters to tens via symmetry compilation or learning dense, non-sparse Clifford-structured Hamiltonians.

themes.title: Quantum Hardware & Experimental Diagnostics
themes.body: Advances in physical quantum platforms showcase atomic-layer passivation to suppress spectral diffusion in silicon T centers alongside optical-lattice quantum coherence microscopy exploiting the Talbot effect.

themes.title: Holographic Complexity Dynamics
themes.body: Investigations into Krylov spread complexity for thermofield-double states dual to BTZ black holes reveal late-time quadratic growth rather than standard linear acceleration.

connections.body: Both 2608.08798 and 2608.09912 leverage exact physical or algebraic structure (Hamiltonian symmetries and hidden Clifford symmetries, respectively) to bypass standard complexity bounds in learning quantum states and Hamiltonians.

Papers 2608.09915 and 2608.09913 both advance the algebraic characterization of translation-invariant CSS codes, highlighting structural decoupling and boundary cohomology in toric code generalizations.
